{{Quote|There's an incredibly high amount of minerals and ores, but the Metalsmiths keep their methods a close secret. The important thing is that the Metalsmiths Guild controls all metal production on the planet according to the Vandel-Helm Charter, and if we're going to rebuild the fleet, we need Vandelhelm metal to do it.|[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]]|<ref name="VEA">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040304vandelhelm|text=Vandelhelm: Enemies and Alloys|int=Vandelhelm: Enemies and Alloys}}</ref>}}
The '''Metalsmiths Guild''' was a major trade union on the ore-rich [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Vandelhelm/Legends|Vandelhelm]], whose roots dated back to the original settling of the world. Renowned for creating some of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]'s finest alloys, the Metalsmiths Guild had sole control over Vandelhelm's metal production, which in turn played a large role in shipbuilding galaxy-wide. Vandelhelm's metalsmiths were renowned for their secrecy and superstition, jealously guarding the methods they used to create their alloys and refusing to work without the blessing of the [[Venerated Ones]], who were descended from the original founders of the Guild. Although the Metalsmiths Guild fell under [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] sway during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Alliance of Free Planets]] freed the [[Prison/Legends|imprisoned]] Venerated Ones and removed the Imperial collaborator [[Guild Master/Legends|Guildmaster]] [[Orrk]].

==Description==
{{Quote|The metalsmiths of Vandelhelm are quite superstitios. The Venerated Ones are the last descendants of the two families who ''discovered'' this ore-rich planet. All mining and smelting secrets come from ''their'' ancestors. Without these two, the Guild feels it can no longer produce worthy metals.|Orrk|<ref name="SW98" />}}
The Metalsmiths Guild was the dominant trade guild on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Vandelhelm/Legends|Vandelhelm]], representing the craftsmen who controlled all metal production on the world. The Metalsmiths Guild had a reputation for superstition, specifically surrounding their reverence of the [[Venerated Ones]], the descendants of the guild's original founders. The Venerated Ones were treated essentially as hereditary royalty, and the metalsmiths traditionally stopped working if they were off-planet or withheld their blessing&mdash;openly opposing an edict from a Venerated One was unthinkable to members of the Guild. The metalsmiths of Vandelhelm were also renowned for their secrecy, tightly guarding the methods they used to create their alloys. The Guild was led by an official known as the [[Guild Master/Legends|Guildmaster]], who was elected by popular vote among guild members.<ref name="VEA" />

==History==
{{Quote|It's not as if I offered up the secrets of our smithing techniques. Just reduced the price to the right people, and cut off the wrong people. As long as there are people identifying themselves as Imperial, they don't get metal from Vandelhelm. And the Guild is so preoccupied with the short-term losses from the new fleet that they can't see how much we'll all gain in the long run. Once the Solo fleet is flying, it will increase our stature and our profits, and we'll still helping the New Republic while we're at it. It's not the profitable thing, but it's the right thing.|Lilli|<ref name="VEA" />}}
Extremely rich in valuable metals and minerals,<ref name="VEA">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040304vandelhelm|text=Vandelhelm: Enemies and Alloys|int=Vandelhelm: Enemies and Alloys}}</ref> the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Vandelhelm/Legends|Vandelhelm]] was discovered around the year [[3053 BBY]],<ref name="Vandel">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw200403041vandelhelm|series=Vandelhelm: Enemies and Alloys|text=Part 1: File Vandelhelm-LC/hsnn}} states that [[Vandelhelm/Legends|Vandelhelm]] was discovered 22,000 [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the [[Galactic Constitution Conference|founding]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], which ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]'' dates to [[25,053 BBY]]. Thus, Vandelhelm was discovered in approximately [[3053 BBY]].</ref> by a pair of independent prospectors, [[Vandel]] and [[Helm]]. The two partners' first ore exports from the world that would bear their names were highly profitable, so much so that they used the proceeds to attract many of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]'s best metalsmiths to found the first Metalsmiths Guild, which was granted total control over the planet's metal production by the [[Vandel-Helm Charter]]. The guild persisted for over three millennia on Vandelhelm, driving the industry that made the planet famous for its extremely fine alloys.<ref name="VEA" />

[[File:Guildmaster_orrk.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Guildmaster Orrk, who collaborated extensively with the Galactic Empire.]]
Vandelhelm's importance to the galaxy's shipbuilding industry had only grown by the era of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], when Vandelhelm fell under [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] control. Then-Guildmaster Orrk conspired with the Imperials to arrest the two child Venerated Ones&mdash;[[Lillindri Nanimei Filda Vandelhelm XXXII|Lillindri "Lilli" Nanimei Filda Vandelhelm XXXII]] and her younger brother [[Endrodanar Tiopuld Shaamador Vandelhelm XXIV|Endrodanar "Endro" Tiopuld Shaamador Vandelhelm XXIV]]&mdash;in order to take full control over the Metalsmiths Guild. The Venerated Ones were [[Prison/Legends|imprisoned]] for three years on [[Ord Vaug]] before they were freed by [[Liberation of Ord Vaug|liberators]] from the [[Alliance of Free Planets]], who [[Mission to Vandelhelm|dispatched]] top [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Nien Nunb/Legends|Nien Nunb]] to return them home. The Venerated Ones return to rejoicing from the common guild members, even as Orrk continued plotting against them along with Imperial [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Mordur]]. However, he was quickly discovered and his plans foiled upon the Venerated Ones' return, meeting his end at Solo's hands.<ref name="SW98" />

Immediately after the Venerated Ones' return and Orrk's demise, the Metalsmiths Guild elected the 15-year-old Lilli as the new Guildmaster. Lilli remained forever loyal to the Alliance of Free Planets and the successor [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], and presided over a very generous trade agreement with the government that had rescued her and her brother from captivity. This loyalty took precedence over the Guild's profits, much to the New Republic's benefit&mdash;increased shipments from Vandelhelm played a large part in the New Republic's victory in the [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] [[Thrawn campaign|campaign]]. The increased production came with stagnant income, as Lilli ensured prices stayed down for the New Republic and earned her opposition from some in the Guild.<ref name="VEA" /> 

These rumblings only grew louder in [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]], when Lilli ordered a enormous shipment of alloys to create a new [[Solo-class combat freighter|''Solo''-class combat freighter]]&mdash;in conjunction with the [[Republic Engineering Corporation]], [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub]] and [[Fondor Shipyards/Legends|Fondor Shipyards]]&mdash;to commemorate the 10th anniversary of her rescue by the Alliance. Having grown accustomed to unfettered trade after the end of Imperial control, the hit to profits caused by this undertaking created a strong undercurrent of dissatisfaction within the metalsmiths. This extended to her own brother, who served as her security officer and advisor, and who himself plotted to wrest control of the Guild from his sister and sell the ''Solo''-class ships to the highest bidder. His attempt on her life was foiled by Solo and Nunb, who had returned to Vandelhelm for the launch ceremony.<ref name="VEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Metalsmiths Guild was introduced in [[Star Wars (1977) 98|''Star Wars'' (1977) 98]], written by [[Archie Goodwin]], illustrated by [[Al Williamson]] and released in [[1985]].<ref name="SW98" />
